title: Area Ratio (Sampler Disturbance Index)

Ca.description: Area ratio — measure of soil displacement by sampler wall

D_o.description: Outside diameter of sampler cutting edge

D_i.description: Inside diameter of sampler cutting edge

applicability: Lower Ca = less disturbance. Target Ca ≤ 10% for undisturbed sampling. Shelby tube: ~10–13%. Split-spoon: ~112%. Fixed-piston: ~10%. Hvorslev recommended Ca ≤ 10% for satisfactory undisturbed samples.

title: Inside Clearance Ratio

D_s.description: Inside diameter of sampling tube (above cutting edge)

applicability: Small inside clearance (0.5–1.5%) allows sample to expand slightly, reducing wall friction during push. Excessive clearance (>3%) allows remolding. Zero clearance grips sample — difficult to extract and increases disturbance during extraction.

title: Recovery Ratio

L_sample.description: Length of sample recovered in tube

L_push.description: Length of tube pushed into soil

applicability: R = 100%: ideal full recovery. R < 100%: sample compression (disturbance), loss from bottom, or obstruction. R > 100%: sample swelling or suction drawing extra soil into tube. Acceptable range: 95–105%.

title: Lunne Sample Quality Criterion (Δe/e₀)

e₀.description: Initial void ratio of sample (before reconsolidation)

e_recon.description: Void ratio after reconsolidation to estimated in-situ vertical effective stress

applicability: For OCR 1–2: Δe/e₀ < 0.04 = very good to excellent; 0.04–0.07 = good to fair; 0.07–0.14 = poor; > 0.14 = very poor. For OCR 2–4: limits shift (less strict). Evaluated from oedometer test results.

title: Sample Length to Diameter Ratio
applicability: Recommended L/D ≤ 10 for push samplers to limit cumulative wall friction disturbance. For Shelby tube: 610 mm push / 73 mm ID ≈ L/D = 8.4 (acceptable). Longer samples increase disturbance at top due to wall friction during push.

title: Outside Cutting Edge Taper Angle

D_o.description: Outside diameter at cutting edge (may be slightly smaller)

L_taper.description: Length of tapered section at cutting edge

applicability: Sharp cutting edge (small β, ≤ 5–9°) reduces disturbance. ASTM D1587 specifies cutting edge angle requirements. Dulled or damaged edges dramatically increase disturbance — inspect before every use.
